q.t: Four consecutive numbers add up to 34. What is the smallest?
Put + or − signs between 3, 4, 5, 6 in any way. The answer is always:
q.e: Switching one sign changes the value by twice a number — an even amount — so all eight answers share the same parity, and 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 18 is even.

q.t: Which expression is even for EVERY integer value of the letters?
q.e: 4m + 2n = 2(2m + n) has 2 as a factor. The others change parity with the values.

q.t: Is 7281 divisible by 9?
o: Yes, the digits add up to 18
No, the digits add up to 18
q.e: 7 + 2 + 8 + 1 = 18, a multiple of 9. Each place value is 1 more than a multiple of 9, so only the digit sum matters.

q.t: Is 524 divisible by 4?
q.e: 100 is a multiple of 4, so only the last two digits matter. 24 ÷ 4 = 6.

q.e: LCM(8, 3) = 24 because they are coprime.

q.t: In PQ × 8 = RS (2-digit numbers, different letters = different digits), what is PQ?
q.e: PQ ≥ 13 gives a 3-digit product. 10 × 8 = 80 repeats 0 and 11 repeats 1. 12 × 8 = 96 ✓.

q.t: If p is the greatest of five consecutive numbers, the smallest is:
q.e: Going down from p: p − 1, p − 2, p − 3, p − 4.

q.t: Find the remainder when 7309 is divided by 9.
q.e: 7 + 3 + 0 + 9 = 19 → 1 + 9 = 10 → 1. The digit sum keeps the same remainder as the number.

q.t: What is the remainder when 158 is divided by 11?
q.e: Alternating sum from the units digit: 8 − 5 + 1 = 4.

q.t: Is 90904 divisible by 11?
q.e: 4 − 0 + 9 − 0 + 9 = 22, a multiple of 11. Place values are alternately 1 more and 1 less than multiples of 11.

q.t: A number is divisible by 6 and by 4. Must it be divisible by 24?
q.e: LCM(6, 4) = 12, not 24, because 6 and 4 share a factor 2.

q.t: If a number is divisible by 9 and by 4, it is divisible by:
q.e: 9 and 4 share no common factor, so LCM = 36.

q.t: 661 leaves remainder 3 on ÷7 and 4779 leaves remainder 5. What remainder does 4779 + 661 leave?
31z5 is a multiple of 9. Which values can z take?
q.e: Digit sum 9 + z must be a multiple of 9: z = 0 gives 9, z = 9 gives 18.

q.t: What is the smallest multiple of 9 whose digits are all even?
q.k: min(n for n in range(9,1000,9) if all(int(d)%2==0 for d in str(n)))
q.e: Even digits give an even digit sum, so it must be 18. Two even digits reach at most 16, so we need three: 2, 8, 8 → 288.

q.t: Which multiple of 9 is closest to 6000?
q.e: 6000 has digit sum 6, so it is 6 above 5994 and 3 below 6003.

q.t: How many multiples of 9 lie between 4300 and 4400?
q.k: len([n for n in range(4300,4401) if n%9==0])

q.t: What is the digital root of 9a + 36b + 13 (a, b whole numbers)?
q.e: 9a + 36b + 13 = 9(a + 4b + 1) + 4; multiples of 9 don't change the digital root.

q.t: Pebbles: groups of 2, 3 or 5 leave 1 over; groups of 7 leave none; there are at most 100. How many?
q.k: [n for n in range(1,101) if n%2==1 and n%3==1 and n%5==1 and n%7==0][0]
q.e: n − 1 is a multiple of LCM(2,3,5) = 30: 31, 61, 91. Only 91 = 7 × 13.

q.t: Find the smallest number leaving remainder 2 on ÷3, 3 on ÷4 and 4 on ÷5.
q.k: min(n for n in range(1,200) if n%3==2 and n%4==3 and n%5==4)
q.e: Each remainder is one less than the divisor, so n + 1 is a common multiple of 3, 4, 5. Smallest: 60 − 1.

q.t: Three numbers each leave remainder 2 when divided by 6. Their sum is:
UT × 3 = PUT. What is UT?
q.e: PUT − UT = P00, so 2 × UT = P00, giving UT = 50 and P = 1: 50 × 3 = 150.

q.t: JK × 6 = KKK. What is JK?
q.e: KKK = 111 × K, so JK = 111K ÷ 6. K = 4 gives 74 (which ends in 4 ✓): 74 × 6 = 444.

q.t: Find the remainder when 481 is divided by 11.
q.e: 1 − 8 + 4 = −3, so 481 is 3 short of a multiple of 11, i.e. remainder 11 − 3 = 8.

q.t: If a number is divisible by 7, it is divisible by every multiple of 7. This is:
q.e: 42 is divisible by 14 but not by 28.

q.t: 48a23b is a multiple of 18. How many pairs (a, b) are possible?
q.k: len([(a,b) for a in range(10) for b in range(10) if int('48%d23%d'%(a,b))%18==0])

q.t: 3p7q8 is divisible by 44. What is p + q?
q.e: For 11: 8 − q + 7 − p + 3 = 18 − (p + q) must be a multiple of 11, so p + q = 7 (18 is too big with q even). E.g. 37708 = 44 × 857.

q.t: 8(7b − 3) − 4(11b + 1) is a multiple of 12:
q.e: It simplifies to 12b − 28 = 12(b − 3) + 8, which always leaves remainder 8.

q.t: The product of any 4 consecutive integers is always a multiple of:
q.e: Among 4 in a row there is a multiple of 4, another even number, and a multiple of 3: 4 × 2 × 3 = 24.

q.t: WOW × 5 = MEOW. What is WOW?
q.e: 5 × W ends in W, so W = 5. Trying O = 0…9, only 575 × 5 = 2875 puts O (7) back in the tens place with all letters different.
